why: B5 in the cell. The wall (gain 4, bias -3, fast) senses; four slow adaptation neurons S1-S4 (tau 20) read the wall through front-blind spokes (8 - 8 cos theta, so a run's front beats barely register) and press it back down (-8 each), holding it at a low resting beat (about 0.06) across light up to about 8. F and SL read the same sum with the same bias, F fast (tau 1) and SL slow (tau 3): F - SL is zero in steady light at any level and positive while the light rises, B5's comparison. R1 is a near-critical switch (self link 4.8, bias -2.6) on 8 (F - SL): on above about 0.31, off below about 0.09, so it holds through a run while the light keeps rising. R2 cleans R1's leaky off-state into a real off, and drives the front half of the wall (out -1.4 + 8 cos theta: front nodes beat, back nodes stop; the -1.4 makes the front-blind sum see almost no change from the run itself). No aim: the run goes straight ahead and the rotational noise turns the cell while it waits, as B5.
